acceptable_visual_variants: Two hands gently drifting apart against a soft, warm background
Two paths diverging in a forest with a single footprint at the split
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: Hands slipping away or letting go of each other's physical grasp.
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: An illustrator might draw two literal hands slipping apart in mid-air, which misses the emotional depth of human relationships parting.
metaphor_spans.tenor: People parting ways or separating in life
metaphor_spans.vehicle: Hands letting go of each other

acceptable_visual_variants: A winding dirt path disappearing into a soft sunrise
A fork in a quiet forest trail
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: Physical roads or pathways belonging to life.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation of L3 ('Do the paths of life really change') introduces a negative/questioning tone ('really change') which is not present in the original Hindi text 'जिंदगी के रास्ते बदल जाते हैं' (which simply states that the paths of life do change).

consistency_review_findings.issue: The poem's language is specified as Kannada in the metadata, but the actual text of the original poem, the source spans, and the source terms are entirely in Hindi (written in Devanagari script). This is a fundamental language mismatch.
The translation_quality is marked as 'faithful', but there is a non-empty translation_loss list detailing a significant semantic shift in line L3. This is internally inconsistent.

original_poem:
हाथ छूटे भी तो रिश्ते नहीं छोड़ा करते,  
कभी भी, कहीं भी, किसी भी मोड़ पे,  
जिंदगी के रास्ते बदल जाते हैं।  

दूरियां कभी दिलों को नहीं तोड़तीं,  
हमेशा पास होते हैं वो लोग जिनसे  
हम दिल से जुड़े होते हैं।
poem_title: Hath Chhootey Bhi To Rishte Nahin Chhoda Karte
translated_poem:
Hands may part but relationships endure,  
Never, anywhere, at any crossroads,  
Do the paths of life really change.  

Distances never break hearts,  
Those who are connected to us from the heart,  
Are always near, always with us.
